prompts:
Edit this existing Petani empty-state illustration, keeping the same isometric view, single green tractor, golden paddy, circular soil base and unobstructed dirt lane ahead of the tractor.
Required revisions:
1. Reduce the soil disk's vertical thickness by approximately 30%: its exposed front soil wall should be 70% of its previous height, a visibly thin soil slice.
2. Reduce the circular soil footprint's diameter by approximately 30% relative to the tractor. Keep the tractor itself at its existing size, rather than shrinking everything uniformly. The field should be more compact around the tractor. In the 1000-square image the soil ellipse should be approximately 630-660 pixels wide, centered, compared to the previous roughly 900-pixel-wide base. Preserve the truly circular ground plane projected as an ellipse, smooth curved edge.
3. Make the paddy GRID CELLS LARGER. Use fewer, broader clumps/patches of golden rice with wider regular spacing, straight parallel rows and perpendicular columns. Clear obvious orderly grid, substantially larger cells than before. No tiny densely packed grid. No radial/concentric planting.
4. Completely change coloring/rendering from shiny 3D plastic to beautiful HAND-PAINTED WATERCOLOR / water-based coloring: soft translucent pigment washes, delicate granulation, visible brush textures, softly layered warm ochres and golden yellows, forest-green washes on tractor with base hue #176B45, subtle brown soil, ivory roof. Retain clean readable isometric shapes and detailed recognisable tractor wheels/cab, but matte watercolor texture and gentle hand-painted edges, no glossy 3D highlights. Paper grain may exist INSIDE the painted objects, not as a background.
Keep a broad bare-earth lane at least tractor-width going from underneath the tractor all the way in front of its nose to the lower-right circular edge. Nothing planted in front of tractor; no trees, no pineapples, no people.
Transparent alpha outside the illustration, no white paper rectangle, no colored background, no checkerboard graphic. Square PNG for exact 1000x1000 export. Entire scene visible, centered, balanced margins, no text, labels or watermark.

Refine this watercolor farm image. Preserve the watercolor coloring, tractor design/green color, circular ground, golden paddy, transparent background, and clear lane in front of the tractor.
The circular footprint is STILL TOO LARGE. Make the soil disk diameter another 18-20% SMALLER in the square canvas, keeping the tractor at exactly its current apparent pixel size. This is NOT a uniform scale-down: the tractor must become proportionally larger relative to the surrounding farm. Aim for the soil disk width to occupy only about 65% of the square canvas width, centered. Keep the entire tractor and soil visible.
Use fewer large paddy patches to fit the reduced circular field, spaced in perfect straight parallel grid rows and perpendicular columns. Keep the enlarged grid cells, not dense tiny plants. Keep the bare lane at least tractor-width running from underneath the tractor all the way out through the lower-right edge, with nothing growing directly ahead.
Make the visible front soil rim a modest shallow slice about 3.5% of disk width, not a paper thin edge and not a thick pedestal. Preserve all hand-painted watercolor texture and warm golden rice, no glossy 3D look.
Transparent alpha background with generous balanced margins around the more compact island. Square PNG for 1000x1000 export. No text, no watermark, no other objects.
